findings: The prior failure is addressed: the USD collider audit now uses Prim.HasAPI for CollisionAPI and MeshCollisionAPI checks instead of invalid schema-to-int conversion.

The planned probe is honestly bounded to loaded-reset discovery. It measures native rigid-body/view counts, enabled collider topology, masses, material bindings, fixture contacts, live poses, stability endpoints, and camera validity without claiming full frozen-contract qualification.

The eight media and two washers are authored as independent dynamic rigid bodies with physical convex collision geometry, explicit mass/inertia, unrestricted motion, and no post-reset pose writes, teleports, welds, freezing, hidden forces, or collider disabling.

Contact evidence begins after completed control steps; reset-cleared buffers are retained only as ungraded trace data. Per-body screen contacts remain distinguishable, and 20 Hz measurements are explicitly labeled rather than represented as physics-substep coverage.

The sampled score is derived from live poses, sampled crossing history, conservative receiver containment, and native masses. It is not constant, and the source explicitly excludes this observer from genuine-passage or aggregate qualification claims.
The report and screenshot paths match the workspace-relative executor contract. Both planned source files are syntactically parseable; native results are correctly deferred until execution.
Impact-on-jobs eligibility remains unresolved and must block export, release certification, and Dream, but the authorized prototype exception allows this source preflight to pass.
